item.title: Citizen Developer Level 1
item.description:
Introduction

This is the start of the Agilebase journey. At this level you can create your own customisations, using no coding.

An Agilebase citizen developer can create ‘personal copies’ of views and edit those copies

  • remove or add fields, excepting any used for multi-tenanting (only higher level developers can access those fields)
  • add calculations
  • rearrange fields and change sorting
  • add or remove filters (except on multi-tenanting fields)
  • add and remove charts
  • join in data from other tables

Views used by workflows can’t be copied, and creating brand new views comes at level 2.

item.title: Citizen Developer Level 2
item.description:
Introduction

You are now well on your way through the Agilebase journey.

This level is suggested or ‘unlocked’ once a citizen developer has carried out a certain number of citizen development functions and has therefore started to learn how no code development works in a safe environment.

However to activate the level, it must be manually assigned by a Software Architect level user, as it allows changes to the system which can affect other users.

item.title: Citizen Developer Level 3
item.description:
Introduction

A Software Architect (see below) can, at their discretion, assign a citizen developer 3 ‘develop’ privileges on tables.

The privileges are as per Citizen Developer level 2, but you can also update or remove fields which have visibility rules, and manage data integrity constraints.

Views work in the same way as at level 2.

item.title: Junior Software Architect
item.description:
Introduction

A junior software architect can use practically all of the application building functionality of Agilebase. For example

  • Create workflows (including chasers, document generation)
  • Set up APIs
  • Create, edit and delete roles, apart from the most powerful ones, such as those allowing exports or used for multi-tenanting
  • Assign privileges to roles or users up to the ’edit’ level
  • Work on fields, views etc. created by anyone, on tables they have ‘develop’ privileges for
  • Edit advanced view settings, such as API access, and fields used for multi-tenanting

They can see all tables and views in the system, whether or not they have privileges to see the actual data in them. That allows them to see the whole picture when looking at a system, so that consequences of a change can be seen and the chance of duplicates being made is reduced.

item.title: Software Architect
item.description:
Introduction

As well as building and disassembling applications, software architects can set company-wide settings and manage the account as a whole. They can

  • Add and remove users, and edit their details
  • Edit company level settings (e.g. security settings)
  • View and set other users’ learning levels (Agile Academy)
  • Assign any privileges, and manage any roles

Don’t know where to start?

If your company has just started building using Agilebase and you are reading this, then you’re probably feeling that you’ve been thrown in to the deep end! Don’t worry - using Agilebase will feel like you’ve been given a life buoy on … with an outboard motor… in lovely warm water… next to the 5 star all inclusive Caribbean resort! To kick off, watch the following guide which will walk you through building a fully functional sales CRM.
